tecnicas.observacao: Assistente único da OpenAI Assistant API sobre GPT-4 Turbo (gpt-4-1106-preview) com instruções que especificam formatos de entrada/saída (instrucao, restricoes), prompt do usuário que manda consultar knowledge.txt, recuperação de uma base de 50 problemas da Leetcode com soluções documentadas (contexto, exemplos), análise de semelhanças e diferenças antes do rascunho (raciocinio; Fig. 1 mostra 'Analysis' junto ao código) e laço 'Test-Optimisation' com casos de teste gerados pelo próprio assistente e executados no Code Interpreter até todos passarem (feedback). O contrafactual é o pacote contra a linha 'GPT-4 Single-agent' da Tabela II; o ganho é do pacote, não de um mecanismo isolado. O prompt do GPT-4 sem ferramentas e sua versão não são descritos (nao_informado), por isso os mecanismos acrescentados são inferidos a partir das ferramentas e da base de conhecimento, e instrucao/restricoes não são listadas como acrescentadas. As instruções completas do assistente aparecem truncadas ('...') na Listagem 1. Não é pacote híbrido no sentido de ajuste fino: as ferramentas são recuperação de contexto e execução de testes.

citacoes.trecho: In this study, we present SelfCoder, a self-guided, single-agent framework for code generation utilising the OpenAI Assistant API built upon GPT-4.
By tapping into a comprehensive Python code knowledge base, SelfCoder creates an initial draft and refines it iteratively through a feedback loop using the Code Interpreter tool.
SelfCoder is defined as a code generation assistant with instructions specifying its input/output formats.
The initial generation phase includes creating test cases for the Code Interpreter to assess the quality of the output.
If errors are found, SelfCoder iteratively regenerates the code and reruns the tests until all cases pass.
The codebase includes 50 classic programming problems and optimal Python solutions sourced from Leetcode, addressing lists, strings, dictionaries, and list-nodes.
We require SelfCoder to identify similar problems, analyses similarities and differences with user requirements, and drafts initial code accordingly.

The ablation study results, shown in the last four rows of Table II, highlight the impact of different self-interactive tools.
Incorporating the Knowledge Retrieval and Code Interpreter tools separately enhances the base model’s performance, confirming the effectiveness of the self-interactive mechanism.
However, current LLMs face challenges like code hallucination due to ambiguous task instructions and limited testing mechanisms.
This self-interactive loop relies on internally stored information, reducing hallucinations and ensuring comprehensive access to relevant data.
However, its performance declines on the extended versions, indicating that SelfCoder may still struggle with robustness, especially for extreme and boundary value cases.
Stability is inconsistent due to an apparent fixed temperature setting, leading to unreliable output for identical inputs.
The combined use of Knowledge Retrieval and Code Interpreter tools raises operating costs up to 25 times compared to the base GPT-4 API.
Additionally, the 512MB token cap for knowledge base files in the Assistant API restricts specialised domain development and limits SelfCoder’s accessible information for code generation.
The extended versions, HumanEval-ET and MBPP-ET, add additional test cases to rigorously evaluate robustness.
The multi-agent framework, utilizing multiple GPT agents, outperformed completion models but lagged behind instruct models due to errors in formatting and incomplete code.
